description: Citation grammars extracted VERBATIM from the deterministic-citations lineage (ALR verifier_core/deterministic_splitter.py == engine legalpdf/deterministic_citations.py, md5-verified 2026-07-29) and from toa_maker.py where it diverges — dialects preserved side by side, never merged. Authoring rules: JS-style named groups (added groups are provenance-marked; they wrap existing alternations without changing match semantics); leading (?i) hoisted to table flags; invisible characters stay \uXXXX escapes, visible non-ASCII stays literal. Python compiles with re.ASCII, JS without the u flag.

entries.provenance: splitter.py:12 == deterministic_citations.py:12 == toa_maker.py:83 (_NEUTRAL_RE, all byte-identical). Named groups and the FR->EN court canonicalization map are beaver-authored additions; the groups wrap existing subexpressions without changing what matches.

entries.provenance: toa_maker.py:84 (_CANLII_RE). No splitter counterpart (splitter's _NEUTRAL_RE cannot match mixed-case CanLII).

entries.provenance: splitter.py:14-23 (_REPORTER_RE, three-branch: [year] / (year) / bare-volume, built on _REPORTER_WORDS which is the reporter_words def). Trailing lookahead bounds the match at clause edges. Recall-first routing evidence by design.
toa_maker.py:85-89 (_REPORTER_RE). Dialect vs splitter: single branch, volume mandatory, digits allowed inside reporter words, page \d{1,6}, NO re.I, no trailing clause-edge lookahead.

entries.provenance: toa_maker.py:90-96 (_STATUTE_RE). Dialect vs splitter: CQLR/CCSM hoisted ahead of the two-letter codes, chapter class gains parentheses, and a second branch covers regulations (Alta Reg / BC Reg / O Reg / OIC / SOR / SI / CFR).
splitter.py:30-34 (_JOURNAL_RE). Title class includes U+2019 right single quote.

entries.provenance: toa_maker.py:97-100 (_JOURNAL_RE). Dialect vs splitter: one character — the title class drops U+2019. The Queen’s vector is the discriminating pair.
splitter.py:132-135 (_LEGAL_TITLE_RE). Title class has U+2019, no ampersand.

toa_maker.py:101-104 (_LEGAL_TITLE_RE). Dialect vs splitter: gains ampersand, drops U+2019. Match spans differ across dialects on &-bearing and ’-bearing titles; the differential harness, not these vectors, asserts spans.
